scenes.title: An Indoor Paint Shop
scenes.summary: On rainy Monday morning, M3 sets up cross-breeze airflow in the wide back hallway so F1 and M1 can paint the four shutters indoors.
scenes.intro: Steady Monday rain taps on the courtyard roof at {SHOW}, where four bare wooden shutters lean inside the back hallway. {M3} joins {F1} and {M1} with a roll of brown paper and a small fan. Listen first.
story: F1
Still raining outside, {M1}. Will green paint ever dry indoors by Wednesday?
M3
It will if we lay brown paper here and move warm air down the hall.
M1
Water-based garden paint—low smell, fast drying if the air keeps moving.
F1
Where do we point the small fan, {M3}?
M3
Crack the courtyard transom two centimetres and blow dry indoor air toward it.
M1
Smart! Steady dry air flows past the wood without letting a drop of rain in.
F1
Look at the colour in the tin when I stir it—deep linden-leaf green!
M1
Thin even strokes along the grain, {F1}. Thick paint stays sticky.
M3
First coat before lunch, second coat tonight, rock-hard by Tuesday afternoon!
F1
Hand me the wide brush, {M1}—shutter number one is mine!
M1
Save a small brush for the corners... and somebody watch the door if {M2} walks by.
F1
Too late—here comes {M2} in his clean white Monday shirt!
scenes.outro: With brown paper on the floor and warm boiler air moving gently, the rainy Monday paint shop is open—right as {M2} arrives in a crisp white shirt! See you next time.

scenes.title: Green Glasses
scenes.summary: M2 insists on painting one shutter slat to help, immediately getting a streak of green paint on the reading glasses perched on his forehead.
scenes.intro: Wearing his spotless white shirt, {M2} stops beside {F1} and {M1} in the hallway and reaches eagerly for the small corner brush. Let's listen in first.
story: M2
What a lovely garden green! Give me a brush—the owner must help too!
M1
Boss, you are wearing a snow-white shirt and polished black shoes.
M2
Just three neat slats on the bottom! I have a steady hand, watch!
F1
Careful, {M2}, your sleeve is two centimetres from the wet edge—
M2
Missed my shirt completely! Ha! Wait... my nose itches.
F1
{M2}, don't lift the hand holding the green brush—!
M2
Why are you both staring at my forehead like that?
M1
Because you just painted the left lens of your reading glasses bright green.
M2
My glasses were on my forehead again?! Oh, everything looks like a forest!
F1
Stand completely still! Warm water and a soft cloth—off it comes!
M2
Clean as new! Thank you, {F1}... I think I will go supervise the front desk.
M1
Wise decision, boss. Leave the wet paint to us.
scenes.outro: White shirt spared, green glasses rescued in time, and {M2} retreats safely to dry ground at the front desk! See you next time.

scenes.title: Middle D Sings Again
scenes.summary: On Tuesday morning, M1 reseats the tiny brass pin and tunes the middle strings while F3 tests middle D on the walnut piano.
scenes.intro: By Tuesday morning the rain has cleared, and inside Room 9 {M1} sets down his tweezers beside the open piano while {F3} takes her seat on the wooden bench. Listen first.
story: M1
The new felt bushing is dry and the brass pin sits tight, madam.
F3
Your hands are as steady as a watchmaker's, {M1}. May I try the key?
M1
Go right ahead—gently first, then full weight.
F3
Listen... D! Clear, round, and zero rattle in the wood!
M1
Sounds a tiny bit flat next to the note above it, doesn't it?
F3
You have a good ear, {M1}! Turn the steel tuning wrench a hair to the right.
M1
Right here... tell me when to stop.
F3
Right... there! Hold it! Play a warm G-major chord with me—listen!
M1
Look at that—this old walnut box fills the whole glass room!
F3
Wait until you hear {M2}'s aunt's finished waltz tomorrow afternoon, {M1}.
M1
Let me screw the front panel back on and polish the brass pedals.
F3
Thank you, {M1}. After thirty quiet years, this piano has its voice back.
scenes.outro: Middle D rings clear and true, and the walnut upright piano is ready for Wednesday's big afternoon. See you next time.

scenes.title: Hanging the Green Shutters
scenes.summary: In Tuesday's bright afternoon sun, M1, M3, and F1 hang the freshly painted green shutters around Room 9's arched glass.
scenes.intro: Out in the sunny Tuesday courtyard, {M1} and {M3} lift the dry linden-green shutters back onto their oiled iron hinges while {F1} checks the alignment from the stones. Listen first.
story: F1
Lift the left side half a centimetre, {M3}—now drop it onto the pin!
M1
Solid! Swing it open against the stone wall and hook the iron catch.
M3
Stand back by the courtyard tree, {F1}. How does the colour look in daylight?
F1
Like the room belonged to the tree all along! Green shutters, white arches, warm stone!
M1
Now let us carry twelve folded chairs inside and wipe down the four cellar tables.
M3
I measured the floor plan: four tables inside Room Nine, four outside under the lanterns.
F1
And if it drizzles on Wednesday, twelve guests can still sit warm and dry behind the glass!
M1
Look who is peering down from the upstairs landing—{M2} is beaming!
F1
No green paint on his glasses today either!
M3
All heavy work is finished twenty hours early, {F1}.
F1
Now I only need to write clean café signs and help {F2} in the kitchen!
M1
Don't celebrate yet—check the kitchen first. {F2} has six trays of lemons out.
scenes.outro: Fresh green shutters frame the sunlit glass, the tables are in place, and Tuesday evening kitchen prep begins next. See you next time.

scenes.title: The Welcome Sign
scenes.summary: At the front desk, F1 designs a simple welcome sign and café menu card that M2 and F3 check line by line.
scenes.intro: At the front desk on Tuesday late afternoon, {F1} lays out cream card paper and a black pen before {M2} and {F3}. Let's listen in first.
story: F1
Look at our small wooden sign for the street gate—short, warm, and easy to read.
M2
Read it aloud for me, {F1}, so I hear how a neighbour hears it.
F1
'Room Nine Garden Café — Fresh Soup, Warm Bread, Lemon Tart & Tea — Open Daily.'
F3
And underneath in smaller letters: 'Friday Piano Tea at Six O'Clock.'
M2
My aunt's exact Friday hour right on the gate! That makes me proud.
F1
I also wrote the four prices clearly in big numbers so nobody has to squint.
M2
Even without glasses I can read those numbers from two metres away!
F3
Did you leave a small basket by the door for neighbourhood book sharing?
F1
Right beside the piano—all those clean travel books from the hallway bookcase!
M2
A public café, a neighbourhood reading corner, and live music—every word of the city rule!
F3
Let me go practice the waltz once through while {F2} bakes the tart shells.
F1
I will carry these menu cards into the kitchen and check on {F2}!
scenes.outro: Clear menu cards, shared books, and Friday piano hours bring every piece of the heritage promise together. See you in the kitchen next time.

scenes.title: Watch the Low Stool
scenes.summary: In the Tuesday evening kitchen, F2 reaches for the big copper teapot on the high shelf and twists her right ankle stepping off the low wooden stool.
scenes.intro: In the warm kitchen behind the café corner on Tuesday evening, pastry crusts cool on racks as {F2} climbs onto a low wooden stool to reach the big copper kettle while {F1} enters with the menus. Listen first.
story: F1
{F2}, wait—let me hold that wooden stool while you reach the top shelf!
F2
I climb this little stool ten times a week, {F1}, I just need the big teapot—ouch!
F1
{F2}! Grab my arm! Sit right down on this chair—don't stand up!
F2
Ooh... my right shoe slipped on the bottom rung when I stepped down!
F1
Let me slip your shoe off gently. Can you wiggle your toes for me?
F2
Toes move fine, nothing broken—just a sharp twist on the outside of my ankle.
F1
Keep your foot up on this second chair while I wrap cold ice in a clean towel.
F2
No, no, {F1}! Tomorrow is Wednesday! I have lentil soup and twenty lemon tarts to finish!
F1
If you stand on a swollen ankle tonight, you won't walk for two weeks!
F2
Who will bake Wednesday's fresh bread and lemon curd if I sit in a chair?!
F1
Look around this house, {F2}: you have six pairs of hands and one loud voice!
F2
Wait... you want me to sit on a cushion and boss everyone around?!
scenes.outro: Nothing is broken, cold ice is on {F2}'s twisted ankle, and {F1} already has a rescue plan for Wednesday morning! See you next time.

scenes.title: Ice, Pillows, and Orders
scenes.summary: F1 and M4 prop F2's ankle comfortably on two pillows while F2 writes out step-by-step Wednesday baking jobs for the whole crew.
scenes.intro: Ten minutes later in the café corner, {M4} carries down two soft pillows for {F2}'s ankle while {F1} hands {F2} a clipboard and pencil. Listen first.
story: M4
Two firm pillows under your heel, {F2}, and strict orders not to touch the floor.
F2
Fine, fine—if I cannot stand at the stove, listen carefully to my kitchen rules!
F1
Clipboard ready, Chef {F2}! Who gets the six-o'clock bread dough?
F2
{M4} has strong shoulders—he kneads the morning dough while I watch the timer.
M4
Deal! I used to help my grandmother knead Sunday loaves every week.
F1
And who whisks the lemon curd and chops carrots for the lentil soup?
F2
You whisk the lemons at my elbow, {F1}, and {M3} chops every vegetable to the millimetre!
M4
Believe me, {M3} will measure every carrot cube with a ruler!
F1
What job do we give {M2} so he feels helpful without breaking anything?
F2
Polishing the twelve white cups at the table—far away from switches and paint!
M4
Now drink this chamomile tea and go rest upstairs, {F2}.
F2
Wake me at six sharp—nobody touches my oven without me in that chair!
scenes.outro: With her foot propped high on pillows, Chef {F2} assigns every Wednesday morning kitchen station down to the last carrot! Final scene of Episode 4—let's listen.

scenes.title: One Jar Is Salt
scenes.summary: Late Tuesday night while tidying the counter for dawn baking, M2 refills two unlabeled white ceramic jars—leaving F1 and M1 unsure which is sugar and which is salt.
scenes.intro: At ten o'clock Tuesday night after {F2} goes upstairs to rest her ankle, {F1} and {M1} walk into the kitchen and spot {M2} proudly closing two identical white ceramic jars on the baking counter. Listen first.
story: M2
Good night, team! I refilled {F2}'s two big white jars so everything looks tidy for dawn!
F1
Wait, {M2}—those two white ceramic jars had little paper labels underneath!
M2
Oh, the paper got damp when I wiped the counter, so I threw both labels away.
M1
Tell me both jars held sugar, boss. Please tell me both were sugar.
M2
No, one bag was fine white caster sugar and one bag was fine white sea salt!
F1
Which jar got the sugar, {M2}—the left jar or the right jar?!
M2
Left! Definitely left! ... Or did I turn both jars around when I polished the lids?
M1
If {F1} whisks four spoons of sea salt into Wednesday's lemon tarts, the city clerk will run!
F1
Don't panic—tomorrow at six we taste a tiny pinch on a clean spoon before baking!
M2
Write a big red note right now, {F1}! Wait—who is knocking at the front gate at ten at night?!
M1
Look through the lobby window—a woman in a blue coat holding a city folder?!
F1
Wait—isn't the city clerk supposed to come Wednesday at three, NOT Tuesday night?!
scenes.outro: Unlabeled salt and sugar jars on the counter—and someone carrying an official folder knocking at the gate on Tuesday night! Episode 4 is complete—see you in Episode 5.
